simple: a program talks to the network card directly instead of asking the operating system for every message.
analogy: handing the note to the courier at your own door instead of queuing at the post-office counter.
precise: a design in which the operating system sets up access once (memory, queues, permissions) and the application then submits and completes data transfers by reading and writing queue memory and device registers mapped into its address space, with no system call on the data path.
source: D2 of F5-34 (NVIDIA, "RDMA Aware Networks Programming User Manual" (tier 1 for vendor material; listed in the curriculum's Track F reading): the RDMA architecture overview (kernel bypass, zero copy, transport offload, memory registration)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D3 of F5-34 (rdma-core project, header infiniband/verbs.h as installed by the Ubuntu package libibverbs-dev version 50.0-2ubuntu0.2 (tier 2: the project's own published interface)) — opened in this build

simple: the bytes go from your memory to the wire, and from the wire into the other program's memory, without being copied into another buffer on the way.
analogy: nobody copies Wei's note onto a form; the courier carries the original.
precise: a transfer in which the device reads the payload by DMA directly from the sender's application buffer and writes it by DMA directly into the receiver's application buffer, so the CPU makes no intermediate copy; the buffers must stay valid and resident until the transfer completes.
source: D2 of F5-34 (NVIDIA, "RDMA Aware Networks Programming User Manual" (tier 1 for vendor material; listed in the curriculum's Track F reading): the RDMA architecture overview (kernel bypass, zero copy, transport offload, memory registration)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D1 of F5-34 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum reading-list item 81, with its RoCE v2 annex): the architecture overview (channel adapters, queue pairs, transport services, RDMA operations, memory registration and keys)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the network card itself does the work of a protocol like TCP: numbering packets, acknowledging, resending.
analogy: the courier service, not Wei, makes sure the note arrives and fetches a receipt.
precise: implementing the reliable transport (segmentation, sequence numbers, acknowledgements, retransmission, ordering) in the network adapter's hardware and firmware instead of in the host operating system; InfiniBand and RoCE define such a transport.
source: D1 of F5-34 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum reading-list item 81, with its RoCE v2 annex): the architecture overview (channel adapters, queue pairs, transport services, RDMA operations, memory registration and keys)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an operation where only one computer's program takes part; the other computer's card does the work alone.
analogy: the note lands on Amara's shelf while Amara keeps cooking.
precise: an RDMA READ or RDMA WRITE (and atomic operations), which name a remote address and a remote key; the target adapter executes it against registered memory without the target application posting a request or receiving a completion. Two-sided operations (SEND matched with a posted RECEIVE) involve both programs.
source: D1 of F5-34 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum reading-list item 81, with its RoCE v2 annex): the architecture overview (channel adapters, queue pairs, transport services, RDMA operations, memory registration and keys)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D2 of F5-34 (NVIDIA, "RDMA Aware Networks Programming User Manual" (tier 1 for vendor material; listed in the curriculum's Track F reading): the RDMA architecture overview (kernel bypass, zero copy, transport offload, memory registration)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the time a program loses each time it asks the operating system to do something.
analogy: the wait at the counter, however short the road.
precise: the time and CPU work of entering the kernel, doing the requested work (here: copying bytes and running the protocol), and returning; plus, when a thread must wait, the cost of putting it to sleep and waking it up. Measured in this chapter as a difference between two paths, not as a property of any product.

simple: a program that discovers an InfiniBand network, gives every port an address and tells every switch where to send each address.
analogy: the railway's timetable office that numbers the stations and sets the junctions.
precise: the InfiniBand management entity that sweeps the subnet, assigns a local identifier to each port, computes routes and programs the switches' forwarding tables; a port learns the SM's own LID (the installed verbs header exposes it as sm_lid in struct ibv_port_attr).
source: D1 of F5-35 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum reading-list item 81): architecture overview, link layer (local route header, virtual lanes, credit-based flow control, VCRC), network layer (GRH, GID), transport layer (BTH, RETH, AETH, ICRC, transport services, PSNs, ACK/NAK and retransmission), subnet management) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D3 of F5-35 (rdma-core project, headers infiniband/verbs.h and infiniband/opcode.h as installed by Ubuntu package libibverbs-dev 50.0-2ubuntu0.2 (tier 2)) — opened in this build

simple: two kinds of address: a short one used inside one InfiniBand network, and a long one that works everywhere (on RoCE it is built from the IP address).
analogy: a station number on the local railway, and a full postal address.
precise: the local identifier (LID) is a 16-bit address assigned by the subnet manager and used by switches inside a subnet; the global identifier (GID) is a 128-bit address carried in a Global Route Header, required for routing between subnets and, on RoCE, used for every packet. The verbs header declares uint16_t lid and union ibv_gid with 16 raw bytes.
source: D1 of F5-35 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum reading-list item 81): architecture overview, link layer (local route header, virtual lanes, credit-based flow control, VCRC), network layer (GRH, GID), transport layer (BTH, RETH, AETH, ICRC, transport services, PSNs, ACK/NAK and retransmission), subnet management) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D3 of F5-35 (rdma-core project, headers infiniband/verbs.h and infiniband/opcode.h as installed by Ubuntu package libibverbs-dev 50.0-2ubuntu0.2 (tier 2)) — opened in this build

simple: the 12-byte label on every RDMA packet: what kind of packet it is, which queue pair it is for, and its sequence number.
analogy: the courier's own label inside the envelope: "parcel 5 for shelf-desk 0x11".
precise: the InfiniBand transport header present in every packet: opcode, solicited-event and migration bits, pad count, header version, partition key, destination queue pair number (24 bits), acknowledge-request bit and packet sequence number (24 bits); decoded field by field by tshark in this chapter's lab.
source: D1 of F5-35 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum reading-list item 81): architecture overview, link layer (local route header, virtual lanes, credit-based flow control, VCRC), network layer (GRH, GID), transport layer (BTH, RETH, AETH, ICRC, transport services, PSNs, ACK/NAK and retransmission), subnet management) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D4 of F5-35 (The Wireshark project, TShark (Wireshark) 4.2.2 as packaged by Ubuntu, its InfiniBand dissector (tier 4: "what this implementation does"). Run in this build: field names and decodings in R2 and R4, decode table in R3) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the number of each packet on a connection, so the receiver can spot a missing one.
analogy: numbering parcels 100, 101, 102… so a missing 102 is noticed when 103 arrives.
precise: a 24-bit counter in the BTH; for reliable service the responder expects PSNs in order, acknowledges them, and reports a gap with a negative acknowledgement (NAK, PSN sequence error) carrying the expected PSN.
source: D1 of F5-35 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum reading-list item 81): architecture overview, link layer (local route header, virtual lanes, credit-based flow control, VCRC), network layer (GRH, GID), transport layer (BTH, RETH, AETH, ICRC, transport services, PSNs, ACK/NAK and retransmission), subnet management) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R4 of F5-35 (university/labs/F5-35/incast.log, incast_capture.log, nak_detail.log) — run in this build

simple: two ways of carrying InfiniBand's transport over Ethernet: v1 directly inside Ethernet frames, v2 inside UDP/IP packets so routers can forward it.
analogy: v1 couriers stay on the roads of one town; v2 couriers use full postal addresses and can cross between towns.
precise: RoCE v1 places the GRH and transport headers directly after an Ethernet header with its own EtherType (0x8915 as decoded by tshark); RoCE v2 replaces the GRH by an IPv4 or IPv6 header and a UDP header whose destination port identifies RoCE (4791 in tshark's decode table), so packets are routable at layer 3.
source: D2 of F5-35 (InfiniBand Trade Association, the RoCE v2 annex to the InfiniBand Architecture Specification (tier 1; curriculum item 81 names it "RoCE v2 annex"): encapsulation in UDP/IP, UDP port, ICRC for RoCE) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D4 of F5-35 (The Wireshark project, TShark (Wireshark) 4.2.2 as packaged by Ubuntu, its InfiniBand dissector (tier 4: "what this implementation does"). Run in this build: field names and decodings in R2 and R4, decode table in R3) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R3 of F5-35 (university/labs/F5-35/decodes.log) — run in this build

simple: the largest amount of message data that one RDMA packet carries on a connection.
analogy: the largest parcel the courier's van takes in one trip; longer notes are split.
precise: the InfiniBand MTU chosen per connection from 256, 512, 1024, 2048 or 4096 bytes (the values of enum ibv_mtu in the installed header), counting payload only; on RoCE, the packet with all its headers must also fit the Ethernet MTU of every link on the path.
source: D1 of F5-35 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum reading-list item 81): architecture overview, link layer (local route header, virtual lanes, credit-based flow control, VCRC), network layer (GRH, GID), transport layer (BTH, RETH, AETH, ICRC, transport services, PSNs, ACK/NAK and retransmission), subnet management) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D3 of F5-35 (rdma-core project, headers infiniband/verbs.h and infiniband/opcode.h as installed by Ubuntu package libibverbs-dev 50.0-2ubuntu0.2 (tier 2)) — opened in this build; R1 of F5-35 (university/labs/F5-35/roce_packet.log) — run in this build

term: Lossless traffic class and priority flow control (PFC)
simple: a setting that makes an Ethernet switch tell the sender "wait" instead of throwing packets away when one class of traffic fills its buffer.
analogy: the painted lane with traffic lights.
precise: Ethernet priority-based flow control pauses transmission of one priority (traffic class) on a link when the receiver's buffer for that priority passes a threshold; packets are mapped to priorities by a VLAN priority field or by the IP DSCP value; RoCE deployments commonly put RDMA traffic in such a class.
source: D5 of F5-35 (IEEE 802.1Q, its clauses on priority-based flow control and enhanced transmission selection (tier 1); IETF RFCs on the Differentiated Services field and on Explicit Congestion Notification for IP (tier 1)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D6 of F5-35 (NVIDIA, "RDMA Aware Networks Programming User Manual" (tier 1 for vendor material) and the RoCE configuration documentation of the adapter in use (to be named in the dossier): RoCE deployment, lossless configuration, congestion control) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: after a lost packet, resend that packet and every packet after it, even those that arrived.
analogy: the courier who lost parcel 102 redelivers 102, 103, 104 and 105.
precise: a retransmission scheme in which the receiver accepts only in-order packets and discards later ones after a gap, and the sender, on a NAK or timeout, resumes from the first missing sequence number; the reliable-connection recovery assumed in this chapter's forensic lab and in the model of F5-37.
source: D1 of F5-35 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum reading-list item 81): architecture overview, link layer (local route header, virtual lanes, credit-based flow control, VCRC), network layer (GRH, GID), transport layer (BTH, RETH, AETH, ICRC, transport services, PSNs, ACK/NAK and retransmission), subnet management) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
related: Lossless traffic class and priority flow control (PFC)

simple: the list of operations a program can ask an RDMA adapter to do, and the C library that offers them.
analogy: the courier company's rulebook and forms.
precise: the abstract interface the InfiniBand architecture defines between a consumer and a channel adapter; on Linux it is implemented by the rdma-core library libibverbs (header infiniband/verbs.h, functions prefixed ibv_) with per-device user-space providers.
source: D1 of F5-36 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 81): the software transport verbs chapter (protection domains, memory registration, keys and access rights, queue pairs and their states and attributes, work requests and completions, RNR, error handling and flushing), transport services) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D3 of F5-36 (rdma-core project, header infiniband/verbs.h as installed by Ubuntu package libibverbs-dev 50.0-2ubuntu0.2 (tier 2)) — opened in this build

simple: a group that memory regions and queue pairs belong to; a queue pair can only use memory of its own group.
analogy: one household's key ring: keys from another household's ring do not open your shelves.
precise: a verbs object (struct ibv_pd, from ibv_alloc_pd) that associates queue pairs, memory regions and other objects; the adapter allows a work request to use a memory region only if both belong to the same protection domain.
source: D1 of F5-36 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 81): the software transport verbs chapter (protection domains, memory registration, keys and access rights, queue pairs and their states and attributes, work requests and completions, RNR, error handling and flushing), transport services) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D3 of F5-36 (rdma-core project, header infiniband/verbs.h as installed by Ubuntu package libibverbs-dev 50.0-2ubuntu0.2 (tier 2)) — opened in this build

simple: two numbers you get when you register memory: one you use yourself, one you give to the other side.
analogy: Amara's own key, and the key card she posts to Wei.
precise: the local key, placed in a scatter/gather element to let the local adapter access the region, and the remote key, sent to a peer and carried in the RETH of RDMA READ/WRITE so the remote adapter can check access; both are fields of struct ibv_mr.
source: D1 of F5-36 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 81): the software transport verbs chapter (protection domains, memory registration, keys and access rights, queue pairs and their states and attributes, work requests and completions, RNR, error handling and flushing), transport services) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D3 of F5-36 (rdma-core project, header infiniband/verbs.h as installed by Ubuntu package libibverbs-dev 50.0-2ubuntu0.2 (tier 2)) — opened in this build

simple: what a registered region allows: may the adapter write into it locally, may remote peers write or read it.
analogy: what the key card permits: put things on the shelf, or also take them.
precise: bits of enum ibv_access_flags passed to ibv_reg_mr: in the installed header IBV_ACCESS_LOCAL_WRITE = 1, IBV_ACCESS_REMOTE_WRITE = 2, IBV_ACCESS_REMOTE_READ = 4, IBV_ACCESS_REMOTE_ATOMIC = 8, among others.
source: D3 of F5-36 (rdma-core project, header infiniband/verbs.h as installed by Ubuntu package libibverbs-dev 50.0-2ubuntu0.2 (tier 2)) — opened in this build; D1 of F5-36 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 81): the software transport verbs chapter (protection domains, memory registration, keys and access rights, queue pairs and their states and attributes, work requests and completions, RNR, error handling and flushing), transport services) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a slip that tells the adapter what to do (send, receive, write) and where the bytes are.
analogy: the slip Wei puts in his "to send" tray.
precise: struct ibv_send_wr or struct ibv_recv_wr posted with ibv_post_send/ibv_post_recv; it carries a 64-bit wr_id chosen by the program, an opcode (send queue only), flags, and a list of struct ibv_sge entries (address, length, lkey).
source: D3 of F5-36 (rdma-core project, header infiniband/verbs.h as installed by Ubuntu package libibverbs-dev 50.0-2ubuntu0.2 (tier 2)) — opened in this build

simple: the receipt for a finished work request, with "success" or an error.
analogy: the receipt in the receipts box.
precise: struct ibv_wc returned by ibv_poll_cq, carrying the wr_id, a status from enum ibv_wc_status (IBV_WC_SUCCESS, IBV_WC_REM_ACCESS_ERR, IBV_WC_RNR_RETRY_EXC_ERR, IBV_WC_WR_FLUSH_ERR, …), the opcode and the byte count.
source: D3 of F5-36 (rdma-core project, header infiniband/verbs.h as installed by Ubuntu package libibverbs-dev 50.0-2ubuntu0.2 (tier 2)) — opened in this build

simple: a queue pair moves through steps (reset, initialised, ready to receive, ready to send) before it can be used, and falls into an error step when something goes wrong.
analogy: registering the trays, swapping numbers on the phone, then opening for business.
precise: the states of enum ibv_qp_state (IBV_QPS_RESET, INIT, RTR, RTS, SQD, SQE, ERR), changed with ibv_modify_qp and an attribute mask naming which fields of struct ibv_qp_attr are valid.
source: D1 of F5-36 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 81): the software transport verbs chapter (protection domains, memory registration, keys and access rights, queue pairs and their states and attributes, work requests and completions, RNR, error handling and flushing), transport services) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D3 of F5-36 (rdma-core project, header infiniband/verbs.h as installed by Ubuntu package libibverbs-dev 50.0-2ubuntu0.2 (tier 2)) — opened in this build

simple: a SEND arrived but the other side had not posted a receive buffer.
analogy: a letter arrives and Amara has no empty envelope in her "to receive" tray.
precise: the responder's negative acknowledgement for a SEND that finds no posted receive work request; the requester retries after a timer, up to the queue pair's RNR retry count, and then completes the work request with IBV_WC_RNR_RETRY_EXC_ERR.
source: D1 of F5-36 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 81): the software transport verbs chapter (protection domains, memory registration, keys and access rights, queue pairs and their states and attributes, work requests and completions, RNR, error handling and flushing), transport services) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D3 of F5-36 (rdma-core project, header infiniband/verbs.h as installed by Ubuntu package libibverbs-dev 50.0-2ubuntu0.2 (tier 2)) — opened in this build

simple: swapping the connection details over some other channel before RDMA can be used.
analogy: the one slow phone call to swap tray numbers.
precise: transfer of queue-pair number, first PSN, LID and/or GID (and, for one-sided operations, buffer address, length and rkey) through a channel that already works, such as a TCP socket, before the queue pairs are moved to RTR and RTS; the rdma-cm library (librdmacm) automates this.

simple: a set of small programs that measure how fast RDMA is between two machines.
analogy: the courier company's official stopwatch kit.
precise: an open-source benchmark suite distributed with or alongside rdma-core: one program per operation and metric (for example ib_write_lat, ib_write_bw, ib_send_lat, ib_send_bw, ib_read_lat, ib_read_bw), each run as a server on one host and a client on the other.
source: D1 of F5-37 (The perftest project (linux-rdma), README and the programs' --help output (tier 2): program names, server/client usage, flags, output columns, measurement method) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R4 of F5-37 (university/labs/F5-37/perftest_check.log) — run in this build

simple: a latency test sends one message and waits for the answer, many times; a bandwidth test sends many messages without waiting and counts bytes per second.
analogy: one letter there and back, versus a lorry-load.
precise: a latency test is a ping-pong with one message in flight, reporting one-way latency as half the round-trip time; a bandwidth test keeps a window of messages in flight in one direction and reports bytes delivered divided by elapsed time, and the message rate.
source: D1 of F5-37 (The perftest project (linux-rdma), README and the programs' --help output (tier 2): program names, server/client usage, flags, output columns, measurement method) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F5-37 (university/labs/F5-37/bench_tcp.log (sanitizer build, by run_lab.sh) and bench_O2.log (g++ -std=c++20 -O2, by the lab's run.sh)) — run in this build

simple: how many messages per second can be sent, whatever their size.
analogy: parcels per hour, not kilograms per hour.
precise: messages completed per second in a bandwidth test (bandwidth divided by message size); for small messages it, not bytes per second, is the limiting figure.
source: R1 of F5-37 (university/labs/F5-37/bench_tcp.log (sanitizer build, by run_lab.sh) and bench_O2.log (g++ -std=c++20 -O2, by the lab's run.sh)) — run in this build

simple: the useful bytes delivered per second, not counting headers or bytes sent twice.
analogy: the letters that arrived the first time, not the envelopes or the repeats.
precise: application payload delivered once divided by time, or as a fraction of the bytes the link carried; it falls with per-packet header overhead (small path MTU) and with retransmission.

simple: the data path is the work done for every message; the control path is the set-up done once or rarely.
analogy: handing over each letter, versus signing up with the courier company.
precise: in kernel-bypass designs the control path (opening the device, registering memory, creating and connecting queue pairs) goes through the kernel with system calls, while the data path (posting work requests, ringing doorbells, polling completions) runs in user space without system calls.

simple: the most memory a process is allowed to pin so that it cannot be swapped or moved.
analogy: how many shelves you may bolt to the wall.
precise: the per-process resource limit that bounds memory locked with mlock and, on Linux, memory pinned by RDMA registration for unprivileged processes; read with getrlimit(RLIMIT_MEMLOCK) (soft and hard values).

simple: what a program does while it waits for the next message: keep checking, or sleep.
analogy: stand at the window, or nap and ask to be woken.
precise: the choice between busy polling (lowest latency, one core fully used), blocking on a notification such as a completion channel, eventfd or futex (no CPU while idle, a wake-up latency per message), and hybrids that spin for a bounded time and then block; a timed sleep in a polling loop is a poor hybrid because sleep durations are not precise.

simple: a library's memory of which buffers are already registered, so it does not register them again.
analogy: a list of shelves that already have a courier key.
precise: a cache in communication libraries (MPI implementations, UCX, NCCL) mapping user buffers to existing memory regions, to avoid the cost of ibv_reg_mr per message; it must be invalidated when memory is freed or remapped.
source: D3 of F5-38 (NVIDIA, "RDMA Aware Networks Programming User Manual" and GPUDirect RDMA documentation (curriculum items 81, 82); UCX and Open MPI documentation on memory registration caches (curriculum item 83) (tier 1 for vendor material, tier 2 for projects)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: adding a record to the end of a log that is kept as identical copies on several machines.
analogy: Amara writes each diary entry and posts copies to two friends; an entry counts once most of the copies have arrived.
precise: the leader writes entry i to the log of each follower, and the entry is committed when a quorum (for example, a majority including the leader) has stored it; the operation underneath primary-backup replication and consensus protocols (DS301).
source: D4 of F5-38 (Curriculum Track F, milestone F5 (build and accept text) and the DS401 course card; DS301 chapters on replication and quorums (university internal)) — opened in this build
